title: iOS 27 Simulator on x86-64 Linux
summary: Apple's arm64-only iOS 27 Simulator runtime, unmodified, translated to x86-64 on the fly by an embedded JIT (dynarmic) inside Darling. No Mac at runtime. Graphics, input and networking go to native Linux services.
now: Speed 4 running: fixing the fast native-call return (fuse_svc_ret, off since it hung boot) and starting ahead-of-time translation of the iOS shared libraries so first app launches skip translating. Speed 3 landed: boot to home 71 s (was 186 s), Settings 31 s first open / 5 s reopen.
metrics: ~20% translating code, rest running it; AOT translation is next
was ~30.6 s; persistent JIT cache keeps translated code
~50 fps; p50 16.7 ms; latency p50 ~23 ms
goal under 1 GB per app; JIT metadata is ~46%

stages.name: 0. Proof of concept
stages.detail: Small arm64 iOS-simulator programs run on x86-64 Linux under dynarmic. 2.45x slower than native x86 overall; calls into native x86 code cost nothing.

stages.name: 1. Inside Darling
stages.detail: Darling's loader hands arm64 programs to the JIT. Apple's own dyld_sim maps the iOS 27 shared cache; libobjc and libswiftCore run translated. System calls go through native x86 libsystem stubs generated from the cache.

stages.name: 2. Boot to the home screen
stages.detail: launchd_sim → daemons → backboardd → SpringBoard, all arm64 under the JIT, software rendering. Fixed: native malloc, signal delivery, per-thread data, tagged pointers, FP16 instructions, thread cleanup, memory-range exhaustion.

stages.name: 3. Fast and lean
stages.detail: Done: shared cache, slim-park, idle CPU, Metal CA home+Settings, openurl/nsurlsessiond, launch breakdown, svc objc_msgSend experiment (opt-in; inlined next). Next: persistent JIT cache, inlined objc_msgSend, Preferences spin, AOT. Speed 3: inline objc_msgSend and a persistent JIT cache are on; boot 71 s, Settings reopen 5 s.

stages.name: 4. Near native
stages.detail: Translate the fixed iOS 27 shared cache to x86 ahead of time, once per iOS version (like Rosetta 2), with the JIT as fallback.

issues: fuse_svc_ret (cheap native-call return) hangs boot at the Apple logo; off by default while it's fixed (Speed 4)
First app launch ~30 s: needs ahead-of-time translation of the shared libraries (Speed 4)
